title: Japan Voted Condé Nast's 'Top Country'
paragraphs: For the fourth consecutive year, Japan has been voted the best country in the world by readers of the American travel magazine Condé Nast Traveler.

The results of the magazine's 2026 Readers' Choice Awards were announced in October 2026. According to the Japan National Tourism Organization, the magazine received more than 798,000 survey responses from readers in the United States, who rated destinations, hotels and other travel experiences around the world. Because the winners are chosen entirely by readers' votes rather than by the magazine's editors, the results show which places travelers themselves enjoyed most. Japan has now topped the list of countries every year since 2023.

Japanese cities also performed well in the awards. Tokyo was ranked second on the list of the world's best big cities, while Kyoto came 10th. In addition, Japan was ranked fourth in a separate category for the world's best countries for food, receiving a score of 96 from readers.
Highlights from the awards are being featured in the November 2026 issue of Condé Nast Traveler.

Japan's strong performance reflects its enormous popularity with international travelers in recent years. In 2025, the country received a record number of foreign visitors, and many of them were attracted by its food, culture, safety and efficient public transportation.

However, this popularity has also brought challenges. In some popular destinations, such as Kyoto, large numbers of tourists have caused overcrowding, and local residents have complained about problems such as crowded buses and bad manners. As a result, the government and local authorities have been looking for ways to spread tourists more evenly around the country, including encouraging visitors to explore lesser-known regions.
